_about: Answer-key repairs for the FoM bank, applied by tools/key_fixes.py after the extractors. Each entry names what the source said, what the lecture supports, and why. Written 2026-10-14 by the FoM class rep from the existing 'The key looks wrong' flags, which had been explaining the error without changing what the bank scored against.

b4-w14-new-q2-2.why: 01 - Transmission of Infectious Agents puts C. difficile under direct contact and botulism under common vehicle, so I and IV cannot share a letter.

b3-wb-heme-q26.why: The workbook key gives A, C, D, F, so the question is now scored as a select-all instead of shown as a self-marked answer.

b2-w7-new-q15-15.stem: Which are essential components of a preventative health visit for older adults?
b2-w7-new-q15-15.lead: The correct answer is E. The periodic health encounter for older adults runs on ALBUS: Acute issues and safety, Labs and vitals, Book follow-up, Update profile, Screening. Acute issues (A) and screening (C) are both in it. The MoCA (B) is not: the lecture advises against screening asymptomatic older adults for cognitive impairment. A "basic overall risk assessment" (D) is not one of the ALBUS components.
b2-w7-new-q15-15.why: The bank asked which are essential components "except" and keyed E, "A and C", which its own explanation calls essential. 02 - Periodic Health Encounter for Older Adults puts acute issues (A) and screening (C) in ALBUS, so the stem now asks which are essential, matching the key. Reader report #210.

option.E: More blood volume exists in veins than in arteries

b2-w5-meds2024-q18-18.why: Two options were false: D (pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood) and E, since the veins are the capacitance vessels and hold most of the blood volume (about 70%). E now states that correctly, so D is the one false statement, as the explanation intends. Reader reports #250 and #254.

option.E: Noncompetitive antagonists reduce the efficacy (maximal effect) of an agonist but leave its potency unchanged.

b2-w8-meds2024-q5-5.why: Option E had potency and efficacy the wrong way round, so two definitions were incorrect. 03 - Pharmacodynamics: a non-competitive antagonist decreases efficacy (Emax) and does not change potency (EC50). E now says that, so C is the one incorrect definition. Reader report #252.

options: Cervical cancer for low-risk individuals is screened for using an HPV test
Colorectal cancer for low-risk individuals is screened for using a Fecal immunohistochemical test (FIT)
Breast cancer for low-risk individuals is screened for using a mammogram
Prostate cancer for low-risk individuals is screened for using a PSA (prostate-specific antigen) test.
b2-w6-meds2024-q15-15.why: The colorectal option had been split across two letters, which pushed PSA to E while the key still said D, so the bank marked mammography as the answer. The options are rejoined; D is PSA again, as the explanation says. Reader report #258. Option A said Pap test, but Ontario replaced the Pap test with HPV testing in March 2025 (07 - Well Person Care and Screening for Cancer: HPV test every 5 years from age 25), which made A a second wrong practice. A now names the HPV test, so PSA is the only option that isn't best practice. Reader reports #325, #327, #336.

options: Cancer at an earlier age than expected
Multiple primary cancers in one person (one person has cancer left breast and right breast)
Multiple individuals with cancer over several generations on the same side of the family
b2-w6-meds2024-q19-19.why: Two options had been split across two letters each, which pushed "All of the above" to F while the key still said D. The options are rejoined; D is "All of the above" again. Reader report #260.

options: Delirium is screened for with a 4-AT.
Depression in geriatric patients is assessed with the GDS.
A diagnosis for MCI requires an objective change in cognition in at least 1 cognitive domain that does not impair functional activities of daily life.
Risk factors for dementia include lower education, hypertension, and obesity.
Effective medication after a diagnosis of MCI can prevent progression toward dementia.
b2-w7-meds2024-q21-21.why: Two options had been split across two letters each, so the key E landed on the dementia risk factors, a true statement. The options are rejoined; E is the medication statement again, which the explanation calls false.

b2-w7-meds2024-q29-29.why: The bank's own explanation says thoracic spinal cord (K): both legs are weak and the arms are normal, so the lesion is below the cervical segments. The key said cervical (J). Reader reports #265, #271 and #275.

b2-w8-meds2024-q11-11.why: The key (C) said CYP450 reactions make drugs more lipophilic; the bank's own explanation says they reduce lipophilicity and increase hydrophilicity. Most Phase 1 oxidation/reduction reactions are CYP450-mediated, which is A. Reader report #273.

b2-w7-meds2024-q10-10.why: The question asks for eight IADLs and the explanation lists them (telephone, laundry, medications, finances, shopping, cooking, housekeeping, transportation), but the bank kept only A and asked it as single-answer. Reader report #276.

options: Prolonged hyperosmolarity can lead to fatal brain swelling.
Less aldosterone will be secreted by the adrenal cortex.
There will be a dramatically increased secretion of renin from the kidneys.
b2-w5-meds2024-q5-5.answer:
The correct answer is C.

Aldosterone signals the kidneys to reabsorb water indirectly, by directly reabsorbing sodium. With the blood already hyperosmolar, the kidneys reabsorb less sodium to keep it from rising further. Hyperosmolar blood draws water out of brain cells, so they shrink rather than swell (B).
b2-w5-meds2024-q5-5.why: The source printed the brain-swelling option twice (B and C). The duplicate is removed, which moves the aldosterone answer from D to C; the answer itself is unchanged. Reader report #329.

option.E: Of the two autonomic divisions, only the sympathetic nervous system innervates blood vessels: vessel diameter is changed by raising or lowering tonic sympathetic firing.

b2-w5-meds2024-q8-8.why: E said constriction and dilation are controlled exclusively by the sympathetic system, which overlooks local and hormonal control. The lecture's point is narrower (02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation: the parasympathetic system does not innervate blood vessels; tone is set by tonic sympathetic firing), and E now says that. Key unchanged. Reader report #313.

option.C: Epinephrine can both dilate and constrict blood vessels, depending on which adrenergic receptor (alpha or beta-2) predominates in that vascular bed.

b2-w5-meds2024-q9-9.why: C now names the receptor type, alpha or beta-2, as the explanation does; the vascular bed only decides which receptor predominates. Key unchanged. Reader report #315.

b2-w5-meds2024-q20-20.stem:
There are several different systems in the human body and all need to be supplied with blood. Which statements below are true?

  1. Endocrine signaling involves secreting hormones into the bloodstream and therefore is a slower signaling pathway than other direct methods.
  2. More red blood cells enter splenic arteries compared to splenic veins.
  3. Half of lymph returns to the cardiovascular system through the right lymphatic duct.
b2-w5-meds2024-q20-20.why: Statement i had been left inside the stem sentence, so the numbered list labelled statements ii and iii as i and ii. All three are back in the list. Key unchanged. Reader reports #289, #309, #311.

option.A: A pre-ganglionic nerve originates from the Intermediolateral horn of the spinal cord at the T1 level and then synapses with the post ganglionic neuron in the sympathetic trunk at the superior cervical ganglion.

b2-w5-meds2024-q24-24.why: A said 'the cervical ganglia'; the postganglionic neurons for the face are in the superior cervical ganglion, and A now names it. Key unchanged. Reader report #317.

b2-w6-meds2024-q6-6.answer:
The correct answer is D.

A known BRCA-1 carrier is high risk, so she is screened through the High Risk Ontario Breast Screening Program: an annual breast MRI together with a mammogram, ages 30 to 69. Mammography alone (A) is the average-risk screen. CT and PET are not screening tests, and choosing wisely argues against them.
b2-w6-meds2024-q6-6.why: The source keyed MRI alone, but the lecture screens high-risk women with MRI as an adjunct to mammography, annually from 30 to 69 (03 - Cancer Genetics; 07 - Well Person Care and Screening for Cancer). D now says both. The explanation also carried a stray line about dysplasia from another question, now removed. Reader report #321.

b2-w6-meds2024-q10-10.answer:
The correct answer is C.

If a cell receives damage to the same gene on both chromosomes this can produce cancer. The first hit can be inherited and the second hit can be acquired through life.
b2-w6-meds2024-q10-10.why: The explanation carried a line about FIT and colonoscopy from another question; it is removed. Key unchanged. Reader report #323.

option.C: A deleterious mutation to one copy of BRCA-1 or BRCA-2 in someone with two normal copies still leaves a functional copy. Heterozygous carriers do not have this advantage.

b2-w6-meds2024-q21-21.answer:
The correct answer is C.

This question refers to the two-hit hypothesis. Someone born with two normal copies has a buffer: one damaged copy still leaves a working one. A carrier of a BRCA-1 or BRCA-2 mutation has only one functional copy, so if that copy is damaged, cancer may result (assuming other genes mutate as well).
b2-w6-meds2024-q21-21.why: C said 'in homozygotes', meaning people with two normal copies, which read as if they carried two mutations. C and the explanation now say it plainly. Key unchanged. Reader report #331.

b2-w8-meds2024-q25-25.answer:
The correct answer is E.

Phase IV is post-marketing surveillance: once Health Canada approves a drug, it keeps being watched for safety in the wider population (09 - Canada's Healthcare System). E describes it as a study of cost-effectiveness and health-system use, which is not what Phase IV is. A to D match the lecture: animal efficacy and toxicity before any human trial, first trials in humans (about 20 to 80 people), first trials in select patients (about 100 to 300), then head-to-head against the standard of care.
b2-w8-meds2024-q25-25.why: The explanation only repeated option E word for word, so it never said what was wrong with it. Rewritten from the lecture; key unchanged. Reader reports #294, #296.

b2-wb-fom-q108.stem: Which of the drugs shown in the graph is the most potent?
b2-wb-fom-q108.why: The workbook's dose-response graph sits beside the question rather than below it and was dropped when the workbook was read in; it is back. Drug A reaches half its maximum at the lowest dose, so the key stands. Reader reports #291, #305, #307, #319, #333.

The correct answer is E.

Dr. Emciel is being a good steward of medical resources by using a more widely available and affordable test first.
b2-wb-fom-q133.why: The workbook's answer line was read as free text, so the question asked readers to mark themselves and flagged E. It is now scored against the workbook key, E. Reader report #302.

b2-w6-meds2024-q18-18.why: 03 - Cancer Genetics gives p53 mutation, a tumour suppressor gene, as the most common route to evading apoptosis, so C describes a real mechanism rather than an incorrect one; none of the other options is contradicted by the lecture either, so there is no answer to score.

b2-w5-new-q9-9.lead: The correct answer is A. All four happen: hyperosmolality releases ADH (i), low volume activates RAAS (iii), and angiotensin II both raises aldosterone (ii) and causes vasoconstriction (iv).
b2-w5-new-q9-9.why: 02 - Introduction to Blood Pressure Regulation lists the responses to severe dehydration (raised osmolality, low volume) as ADH release, thirst, RAAS activation and cardiovascular reflexes, and 10 - Approach to Abnormal Test Results shows angiotensin II raising aldosterone; neither lecture says aldosterone is suppressed, so ii is true as well.

b2-w5-new-q22-22.lead: The correct answer is E. Working tissues - the gut, skeletal muscle and the heart - add CO2 to the blood; the lungs take it out.
b2-w5-new-q22-22.why: 03 - Body Systems Integration: capillaries in the tissues remove CO2 from them into the blood, and respiration moves CO2 from the red cells to the bronchial tree, so the lungs are where CO2 leaves the blood, not where it is added.

b2-w8-meds2024-q6-6.lead: The correct answers are C and D. C: Drug C reaches the full response, so it is not a partial agonist. D: a non-competitive antagonist lowers the maximal response but does not change potency, so it could not turn Drug B into Drug A, which is more potent than B.
b2-w8-meds2024-q6-6.why: 05 - Principles of Clinical Pharmacology: non-competitive antagonists reduce the efficacy of an agonist but do not change its potency. Drug A's half-maximal concentration sits well left of Drug B's, so D is false as well as C.

b2-w8-meds2024-q7-7.lead: The correct answer is C. Reducing a drug's potency raises its EC50 - more drug is needed for half the maximal effect - so BK-562 could not decrease heroin's EC50.
b2-w8-meds2024-q7-7.why: 03 - Pharmacodynamics: potency is the concentration giving 50% of the maximal effect (EC50), and a less potent drug needs more of it, so lower potency means a higher EC50. The key stands; the explanation now says EC50, as the option does.

b2-wb-fom-q107.answer: The correct answer is A. In an older adult any fall matters: falls are one of the geriatric syndromes, and a fall can be the only sign of a serious illness such as an MI, an infection or hyperthyroidism.
b2-wb-fom-q107.why: 01 - Healthy Aging vs. Disease lists falls among the geriatric syndromes and warns that in older adults a fall may be the only presenting sign of an MI, appendicitis, infection or hyperthyroidism.
